chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah, raising it from Abi Abdillah (عليه السلام), said:

While Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) was delivering a sermon upon the pulpit of al-Kufah, a man known as Dhi'lib stood up before him, eloquent in speech and brave of heart. He said, "O Amir al-Mu'minin, have you seen your Lord?" He (عليه السلام) said, "Woe unto you, O Dhi'lib! I would not worship a Lord whom I had not seen."

He said, "O Amir al-Mu'minin, how did you see Him?" He (عليه السلام) said, "Woe unto you, O Dhi'lib! Eyes do not see Him through the sight of vision, but hearts see Him through the realities of iman. Woe unto you, O Dhi'lib! Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in subtlety, yet not described by subtlety; عظِيم in greatness, yet not described by greatness; Great in majesty, yet not described by magnitude; Majestic in exaltedness, yet not described by coarseness."

He is before everything, yet it is not said that anything is before Him; and after everything, yet it is not said that there is an after for Him. He willed things not through resolve; He is all-aware not through device; He is in all things without being mixed with them, and not separate from them. He is Manifest, not in the sense of direct contact; self-disclosing, not through the commencement of vision; far, not by distance; near, not by closeness; subtle, not by corporeality; existent, not after nonexistence.

He is an Agent, not by compulsion; an Ordainer, not by movement; a Willer, not by inclination; Hearing, not by an instrument; Seeing, not by a tool. Places do not contain Him, times do not encompass Him, attributes do not limit Him, and slumbers do not overtake Him. His being precedes times, His existence precedes nonexistence, and His pre-eternity precedes beginning.

By His endowing the faculties with perception, it is known that He has no faculty; by His bringing forth substances, it is known that He has no substance; by His placing opposites among things, it is known that He has no opposite; and by His pairing things together, it is known that He has no companion. He set light against darkness, dryness against moisture, roughness against softness, and cold against heat.

He joins together its mutually hostile things and separates its closely related things; by their separation they indicate the One who separated them, and by their composition they indicate the One who composed them.
And that is His, the Exalted, saying: "And of every thing We created pairs, that perhaps you may take heed."
So He separated between before and after, so that it may be known that there is no before for Him and no after for Him.

Their innate dispositions testify that there is no disposition for the One who instilled them; their temporality informs that there is no time for the One who assigned them time. He veiled some of them from others so that it may be known that there is no veil between Him and His creation. He was Lord when there was no one lorded over, God when there was none worshipped, Knowing when there was nothing known, and Hearing when there was nothing heard.

key_terms.الْأَوْقَاتُ: times, which do not encompass or delimit Allah
key_terms.بِحَقَائِقِ الْإِيمَانِ: through the true realities of faith by which the hearts know Allah
key_terms.قَرِينَ: a counterpart or associate, which Allah does not have
key_terms.لَطِيفُ اللَّطَافَةِ: utterly subtle beyond created notions of subtlety

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali (عليه السلام) describe seeing Allah and His divine attributes?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a profound exposition of tawhid from Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام), affirming that Allah is not perceived by physical sight but known by the hearts through the realities of iman. It negates corporeality, limitation, temporality, and likeness from Allah while showing that the created order, with its opposites and pairings, points to the absolute transcendence and uniqueness of its Creator.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Abu Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) raising it from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘While Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was preaching upon the Pulpit of Al-Kufa, when a man called Zi’lab stood up to him<sup>asws</sup> who was eloquent of the tongue regarding the addressing and was brave of heart. So he said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>! Have you<sup>asws</sup> seen your<sup>asws</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Woe be unto you, O Zi’lab! I<sup>asws</sup> never worshipped a Lord<sup>azwj</sup> I<sup>asws</sup> did not see’.

So he said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineenasws! How did youasws see Himazwj?’ Heasws said: ‘Woe be unto you, O Zi’lab! The eyes do not see Himazwj by the witnessing of the visions, but the hearts see Himazwj by the realities of the Eman. Myasws Lordazwj is the most Subtle of the subtles (but) Heazwj cannot be described by the subtleties; most Magnificent (but) cannot be described by the magnificence; Greatest of the greats (but) cannot be described by the greatness; most Majestic (but) cannot be described by the rudeness.

He<sup>azwj</sup> was before everything, nothing can be said to be before Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and He<sup>azwj</sup> is after everything, nothing can be said to be after Him<sup>azwj</sup>. It is not by thinking that He<sup>azwj</sup> is Aware, nor by a strategy regarding the things. All of these without being mixed with these, nor is He<sup>azwj</sup> apparent from these. He<sup>azwj</sup> is apparent, not by the immediate explanation. He<sup>azwj</sup> Shines, not by the initiation of sight. He<sup>azwj</sup> is remote, not by a distance. He<sup>azwj</sup> is near, not by approaches. He<sup>azwj</sup> is Subtle, not by embodiment. He<sup>azwj</sup> is existent, not after the non-existence.

He<sup>azwj</sup> is a Performer, not by the desperation, and Evaluator, not by the movement, an Intender, not by thinking, a Hearer, not by an instrument, Seeing, not by tools. Neither does a place contain Him<sup>azwj</sup>, nor does the times enclose Him<sup>azwj</sup>, nor do the attributes limit Him<sup>azwj</sup>, nor do the slumbers seize Him<sup>azwj</sup>. His<sup>azwj</sup> Being precedes the time, and His<sup>azwj</sup> existence (precedes) the nothingness, and His<sup>azwj</sup> eternality (precedes) the beginning.

By His<sup>azwj</sup> Giving awareness the awarenesses are recognised that there is no giver of awareness to Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and by His<sup>azwj</sup> Essence the essences are recognised that there is no giver of essence to Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and by His<sup>azwj</sup> Giving opposites to the things it is recognised that there is no opposite to Him, and by His<sup>azwj</sup> Pairing between the things, it is recognised that there is no pair for Him<sup>azwj</sup>. He<sup>azwj</sup> has Construed the light with the darkness, and the dryness with the wetness, and the rough with the coarse, and the coldness with the heat.

He<sup>azwj</sup> is the Composer between the individual things and a Separator between the close things. It evidences by its separation upon One<sup>azwj</sup> Who separated these, and by their composition, upon their Composer.
And these are the Words of the Exalted [51:49] And of everything We have created pairs that you may be mindful.
Thus, He<sup>azwj</sup> separated between the ‘before’ and ‘after’ in order for it to be known that there is neither a ‘before’ for Him<sup>azwj</sup> nor an ‘after’ for Him<sup>azwj</sup>.

The instincts testify that there is no instinct for the One<sup>azwj</sup> Who Created the instincts. It is informed by the creation of time that there is no time for the One<sup>azwj</sup> Who Created time. He<sup>azwj</sup> Veiled some from the others in order for it to be known that there is no veil between Him<sup>azwj</sup> and His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures. He<sup>azwj</sup> was Lord<sup>azwj</sup> when there none being nourished, and a God<sup>azwj</sup> when there were no worshippers, and a Knower when there was nothing to be known, and a Hearer when there was none to be heard’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhaamd ibn abu ‘Abdallah in marfu‘ manner has narrated from Imam abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.

“Once Imam Amirul Mu’minin addressed the people in the Mosque of Kufa from the pulpit and a man called dhi‘lab a very good orator and brave in heart said, “O Amirul Mu’minin, have you seen your Lord?” The Imam replied, “Fie upon you O Dhi‘lab, how would I worship a Lord whom I would not see?”

The man said, “O Amirul Mu’minin how have you seen Him?” The Imam said, “Fie up on you O Dhi‘lab, the eyes are not able to see Him physically but it is the hearts that see Him through the truth of the faith. O Dhi‘lab, my Lord is subtle in subtleties but can not be described by means of subtle matters. My Lord is great but can not be described by means of greatness. His greatness surpasses all greatness but he can not be described by means of such greatness. He is Glorious in His Glory but He can not be described in terms of thickness.

He is before everything and it can not be said that something was before Him. He will be after all things but it can not be said that there is something after Him. He willed the existence of things but not by means of first thinking about it. He comprehends things but not with a great deal of efforts. Things are not mixed with Him and nor is He indifferent about them. He is clearly manifest but not with contacts and changes. He shines but not in the form of being found out with eye sight. He is far but not in the form of distance. He is near but not in the form of nearness. He is very fine but not in the form of physical fineness. He exists but not after nothingness.

He acts but not because of being forced. He measures things but not by means of movement. He wills but not by means of thinking. He hears but not with tools. He sees but not with instruments. He is not contained in place and held up in times. Attributes do not limit Him and slumber does not seize Him. His Being was before the time and His existence was before nothingness. He was before eternity.

His giving the sense awareness prove that He does not have the tools for sensing. His giving substance to the substances is proof that Himself is not a substance. The existence of a contrary to everything is proof that there is nothing contrary to Him. His giving nearness to things is proof that there is nothing similar to Him. He has made the light contrary to the darkness, the wetness to the dryness, the harshness to the softness, the coldness to the heat.

He combines their transgressing and separates their closeness. The separation among things is evidence of the existence of the One Who causes separation in them and their combinations is evidence of the existence of the One Who combines them.
It is jus as Allah has said, “We have created everything in pairs so that perhaps you may take heed [51:49].”
He has made a distinction between the before and after to show that there is no before and after for Him.

The instincts show that the One who created the instincts Himself has no instinct. The time is evidence that there is no timing for the One Who made the time. Things are hidden from each other are evidence that nothing hides them from their Creator. He was the Lord when there was nothing to enjoy His Lordship. He was to be worshipped when there was no worshipper. He had the knowledge when there was nothing to know. He was hearing when there was nothing to hear.”
